theater: 長安京師與涇原入京道

battle.name: 涇原兵變
battle.theater: 長安京師與涇原入京道
battle.brief: 建中四年十月，涇原節度使姚令言率五千邊軍入衛京師，因糧餉不給而夜半哗變，剽掠市井、焚毀宮闕。眾軍推朱泚為主，朱泚稱帝建燕；德宗與妃嬪、諸王百餘人連夜出奔奉天。九月官軍收復長安，朱泚西走奉天，為段秀實陣前擊殺。卡面羅馬重步兵未曾東來，交鋒靠的仍是長槍、勁弩與飢軍變亂。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 涇原兵變的一方是唐廷及其在關中的軍事網絡，另一方是由涇原邊軍發起、並裹挾京師守軍與市井而成立的叛軍。涇原是唐西北邊鎮之一，軍營在今寧夏固原、隆德一帶，節度使姚令言總其軍政；兵員以募自邊地的軍人與屯田戶為主，軍籍歸節度使衙門，糧餉由度支與鎮庫分給，監軍中使在旁監督，軍中另設兵馬使、判官、押牙各職，分領諸營。涇原軍平時是唐廷防禦吐蕃與內地藩鎮的第一道屏障，調兵入衛卻不是常例，既無京師北衙禁軍的編制，也沒有固定的主將與參謀；出征時由節度使自行率領，糧餉就地自籌，進京之後既無接應的營壘，也無人負責供應。叛軍方面，兵變之初只是五千名缺糧的邊軍；攻入城內、劫掠府庫之後，眾軍另推朱泚為主。朱泚原任涇原節度使，天寶末年已罷兵權，後入朝為相，罷相之後留居京師，兵變發生時正無兵柄。叛軍借重他的名望與舊部關係，他則乘亂建號為大燕，而各道節度使多不奉詔，中樞與藩鎮之間的傳令自此大半失效。
countriesEn: One side of the Jingyuan mutiny was the Tang court together with its military network in the Guanzhong region; the other was a rebel force that began as a mutiny of frontier soldiers and then absorbed the capital's guards and the population of the city. Jingyuan was one of the Tang northwestern circuits, its garrison lying around modern Guyuan and Longde in Ningxia, where the circuit commissioner Yao Lingyan held both military and civil command. Its soldiers were for the most part men recruited from the frontier together with tuntian farming households; the company rolls belonged to the commissioner's office, pay and rations were split between the Department of State Finance and the circuit treasury, supervising eunuchs watched the process, and the command structure included a bingmaishi, a judge and a zeya officer, each holding part of the camp. In peacetime the Jingyuan army was the Tang court's first shield against the Tibetan plateau and against the rebellious circuits of the interior, and moving it to guard the capital was not a routine matter: it had neither the establishment of the Northern Gate guards nor a permanent commander and staff. The circuit commissioner led the column himself, rations were raised on the spot, and once the column reached the capital there was neither a receiving camp nor anyone answerable for the supply. On the rebel side, at the first moment of the mutiny there were only five thousand hungry frontier soldiers; after they broke into the city and stripped the treasuries, the men chose Zhu Ci as their leader. Zhu Ci had once been commissioner of Jingyuan, had lost his command at the end of the Tianbao era, had later gone to court as chancellor, and after being removed from that office still lived in the capital, so at the moment of the mutiny he held no troops at all. The rebels turned to him for his reputation and his old ties in the circuit, and he in turn used the disorder to proclaim the Great Yan, while most circuit commissioners refused his edicts and the chain of orders between the court and the provincial commands largely broke down.
people: 關鍵人物集中在皇帝、叛首與數鎮節度使三方。德宗李適在兵變前不久才由梁州還都，此前因李希烈之亂出奔奉天，又轉入梁州，兵變當夜再以百餘人護駕出宮，趨奉天；其後由陸贄等重臣在行在議處軍政。陸贄時為諫議大夫、翰林學士，自奉天之難起便反對與吐蕃硬拼，力主避實擊虛，兵變之後亦力言其病根在徵召無度、糧餉不給，而朝廷自無解決之道。涇原節度使姚令言率軍入衛，兵變當夜死於亂軍，說法不一，或云被亂兵所殺，或云棄屍溝渠；朝廷後以段秀實接掌涇原兵權，段秀實收復清渠、醴泉一線，進軍奉天，以牙笏擊朱泚面，朱泚命衛士斬之，朱泚自此不能復起。河中節度使李懷光、邠寧節度使尚可孤、汾陽郡王郭子儀各率本部兵勤王，李懷光一度迎帝於河中，尚可孤收復京西，郭子儀後統河中、關內之兵直入長安。反叛方的核心是朱泚，他身邊多為長安降官與降將，兵變初期軍中尚無成制，攻掠所得即為軍資，紀律很快崩解；其餘領袖多為軍中粗豪武夫，領兵則無復顧忌。
peopleEn: The decisive figures fall into three groups: the emperor, the rebel leader, and the commanders of the circuits. Emperor Dezong, Li Shi, had returned to the capital from Liangzhou only shortly before the mutiny, having earlier fled to Fengtian during the rebellion of Li Xilie and then gone on to Liangzhou; on the night of the mutiny he once more escaped the palace with a little more than a hundred attendants and rode for Fengtian, and from that temporary seat the ministers around Lu Zhi went on arranging the conduct of the war. Lu Zhi, then remonstrance commissioner and academy scholar, had opposed a direct clash with the Tibetans since the crisis at Fengtian and urged the court to avoid the enemy's strength and strike his weakness; after the mutiny he argued that the disease lay in endless levies and in rations that were never paid, while the court itself had no remedy. Yao Lingyan, commissioner of Jingyuan, led the troops into the capital and was killed by the mutineers on the night itself; the accounts differ, some saying he was cut down by the soldiers, others that his body was left in a ditch. The court afterwards gave the Jingyuan command to Duan Xiushi, who recovered the Qingqu and Liquan line, drove on to Fengtian and struck Zhu Ci in the face with his ivory tablet, whereupon Zhu Ci ordered his guards to behead him, and Zhu Ci was never able to rise again. Li Huaiguang, commissioner of Hezhong, Shang Kegu, commissioner of Binning, and Guo Ziyi, Prince of Fenyang, each led their own troops to the emperor's cause; Li Huaiguang for a while escorted the emperor at Hezhong, Shang Kegu recovered the western approaches to the capital, and Guo Ziyi later took the armies of Hezhong and the interior straight into Chang'an. At the centre of the rebel side stood Zhu Ci, surrounded by surrendered officials and generals of the capital; the rebel army had no regular organisation in the first days, and whatever it seized in the plunder was its military pay, so discipline broke down quickly, and the remaining leaders were mostly hard soldiers of the ranks who led without further scruple.
kits: 卡面所配的羅馬重步兵是公元前二世紀的兵種：分段鎧甲配重盾，列陣時以盾牆承接衝擊，其戰力建立在補充兵源與補給線之上，而不是靠重裝本身。這套東西在公元783年的長安街頭自然不曾出現，它在本卡的作用，是作為一支重步兵體系的樣本，恰好與涇原兵變背後的問題相照。涇原邊軍真正裝備的，是唐代常備軍的模樣：步兵以長槍與唐刀為主，配以角弓、臂弩、蹶張弩等投射兵器，護身有明光甲、札葉甲、網甲與兜鍪，披膊、膝裙、護臂分護上臂與大腿；騎兵多披馬鎧，用馬槊、陌刀與橫刀，玄甲騎兵以黑甲為號。攻城之具，叛軍用撞竿、飛雲梯與巢車，官軍則倚城堞、櫓、拒馬與鹿角柴障；火器方面，唐人已懂得用火矢與油火焚燒城門樓櫓，《太白陰經》一類唐代兵書已載砲具與火藥配方的記載，說明當時技術已觸到爆裂武器的邊緣。運輸與補給靠輜重車隊、廚炊，以及泥地所用的橇運，軍令用驛騎加急傳遞。涇原一鎮的存亡，本來就繫在河套屯田的收成與轉運線上，糧源一斷，裝備再好也無從施展。
kitsEn: The kit on this card is the Roman heavy infantryman, a soldier of the second century BC: segmentary body armour carried with a heavy shield, standing in a testudo to absorb the impact, whose strength rested on the replacement of manpower and on supply lines rather than on the weight of its equipment. Nothing of the kind could of course be found in the streets of Chang'an in AD 783; on this card it serves as a specimen of a heavy infantry system, and it happens to mirror exactly the problem at the root of the Jingyuan mutiny. What the Jingyuan frontier soldiers actually carried was the ordinary kit of a Tang standing army: infantry fought with the long spear and the Tang saber, supported by composite bows, hand crossbows and powerful siege crossbows, and wore mingguang plate, scale and mail armour with a helmet, shoulder pieces, knee skirts and vambraces protecting the arm and thigh; cavalry were commonly armoured horse troopers using the horse lance, the modao saber and the straight saber, the black-armoured riders being known as the xuanjia. For assault the rebels used battering poles, flying ladders and observation towers, while the government side relied on parapets, wooden galleries, cheval-de-frise and antler obstacles; in the matter of fire, the Tang already understood the use of fire arrows and oil-fire against gates and galleries, and military manuals of the kind of the Taibai Yinjing already carried descriptions of stone-throwing engines and of gunpowder formulae, showing that the technology of the period had reached the threshold of explosive weapons. Transport and supply depended on baggage trains, field kitchens and sledge-hauling for muddy ground, and military orders travelled by hard-ridden relay horses. The survival of a circuit such as Jingyuan was tied from the outset to the harvest of the tuntian fields in the Hetao plain and to the line of transport; once the grain source was cut, no amount of equipment could be brought into play.
tactics: 兵變本身是一場夜半發動的都市攻擊，而非兩軍對陣。涇原軍入城後分作數路，先奪城門與坊門，閉合街口以斷絕內外消息；再以火把與鼓噪為號，縱掠市井、破毀官府、闖入宮闕，打開內府與瓊林庫搬取財貨，隨即以得手之物酬賞士卒，於是市井騷然，城內秩序在數個時辰內瓦解。守方幾乎沒有組織抵抗：京師宿衛多為禁軍，兵變前已奉調出城，宮城守卒寥落，守門者或降或散。皇帝當夜出宮城，與妃嬪、諸王及宦者百餘人乘騎就道，經棧道草地疾馳，一日一夜抵奉天，沿途換馬、乏食，抵達後才遇上河中李懷光所率的迎駕部隊。勤王軍的收復過程則回到常規作戰：河中、邠寧及關內各鎮兵先取京西清渠、醴泉一線，掃清燕軍游騎，再以撞竿與雲梯攻城；入城之後約束士卒不得劫掠，朱泚焚宮室而西走奉天，段秀實追及，陣前以牙笏擊其面，隨即同歸於盡。全過程最吃重的一環仍是糧道——叛軍靠掠奪維持，官軍靠屯田與轉運，兩者都經不起持久。
tacticsEn: The mutiny was a night attack on a city rather than a battle between two armies drawn up in the field. After entering the capital the Jingyuan troops split into several columns, first seizing the city gates and the ward gates and closing the streets to cut the city off from the outside world; then, with torches and beating of drums as the signal, they swept the markets, broke into the government offices, forced the palace gates, and threw open the inner treasury and the Qionglin granary to carry off the wealth, paying the soldiers there and then with what they had taken, until the streets were in turmoil and the order of the city collapsed within a few hours. The defenders offered almost no organised resistance: the capital's garrison was mostly the palace guard, which had been sent out of the city before the mutiny, the inner palace was thinly held, and the men at the gates either surrendered or scattered. That night the emperor left the inner palace with the consorts, the princes and a hundred eunuchs on horseback, riding by plank road and open country, and reached Fengtian in a day and a night, changing horses on the way and short of food, and only there did he meet the escort of Li Huaiguang of Hezhong. The recovery of the capital by the government armies returned to ordinary campaigning: the troops of Hezhong, of Binning and of the interior circuits first took the Qingqu and Liquan line west of the capital, swept away the Yan cavalry outposts, and then assaulted the walls with battering poles and scaling ladders; once inside they held the men from plunder, while Zhu Ci burned the palace buildings and fled west to Fengtian, where Duan Xiushi overtook him and struck him in the face with his ivory tablet, and both were killed on the spot. Throughout, the decisive element remained the grain route: the rebels lived on plunder, the government on tuntian and transport, and neither could stand a long contest.
data: 可核對的數字有限，先列確定者。唐德宗建中四年十月，即公元783年11月，涇原兵變發作。出徵規模是五千：《資治通鑑》記姚令言將兵五千自涇原至京師，別有說法作四千上下。涇原軍營至長安的行程約五百公里、千里上下，沒有水運可借，士卒靠兩腳走了數日。兵變當夜，護駕出奔的只有百餘人，隨行馬匹數十。燕國自十月建號，至次年九月唐軍收復長安，佔據京師約九個月；朱泚在位不足一年，於次年十月在奉天被殺。勤王一方的兵力由河中、邠寧、關內、劍南、隴右各鎮湊成，各鎮兵額史無詳載，官軍實際可用者仍以河中與邠寧兩鎮為主。財物方面，叛軍所取內府、瓊林庫及諸寺觀賑廩，數量史書形容為不可勝計，卻無確數可核；雙方兵員傷亡的數目史籍亦不詳。關中連年旱澇饑荒，米價騰貴，軍用與民用爭食，度支左支右絀，這才是數字背後最硬的一條。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and the certain ones come first. The mutiny broke out in the tenth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong under Emperor Dezong of Tang, that is, in November AD 783. The size of the column was five thousand: the Zizhi Tongjian records that Yao Lingyan brought five thousand men from Jingyuan to the capital, while other accounts put the number nearer four thousand. The road from the Jingyuan camp to Chang'an is about five hundred kilometres, a thousand li or so, with no water transport available, so the soldiers covered it on their own legs over several days. On the night of the mutiny the imperial escort numbered only a hundred odd, with a few tens of horses. The state of Great Yan, proclaimed in the tenth month, held the capital for about nine months, until the Tang armies retook Chang'an in the ninth month of the following year; Zhu Ci's reign lasted less than a year, and he was killed at Fengtian in the tenth month. The relief armies were drawn from the circuits of Hezhong, Binning, the interior, Jiannan and Longyou, and the paper strength of each is nowhere recorded, the government's actual force remaining chiefly that of the two circuits of Hezhong and Binning. As for booty, the rebels carried off the inner treasury, the Qionglin granary and the stores of the temples and monasteries, described in the histories as beyond computation, though no exact figure survives; the numbers of men lost on either side are likewise not recorded. In Guanzhong there had been successive years of drought and flood and of famine, the price of rice had risen sharply, the army competed with the people for the same grain, and the Department of State Finance was hard pressed on every side; that is the hardest of all the numbers behind the story.
cause: 起兵的直接原因，是一支被臨時徵調的邊軍在京城找不到糧食。興元元年秋，吐蕃逼境，唐廷徵涇原兵入衛；兵至京師本應由北衙禁軍與太倉供應，然禁軍調發遲滯，府庫因奉天之難與播遷之故空虛，監軍中使與節度使互相推諿，士卒久宿坊郭，冷食無著，怨氣積到極處。兵變當夜，軍士夜入城中求糧不得，遂擊柵鼓噪，一哄而散，中樞與宮禁一時崩解。更深一層的原因在體制：安史之亂後府兵制已壞，邊軍全靠募兵與屯田，涇原地處窮邊，水利與田畝有限，豐年僅能自給，饑年便要仰賴關內轉運；而朝廷自兩稅法之後，軍費浩大，討河北、拒吐蕃兩線並進，度支常常入不敷出，鹽法雖經劉晏整頓，劉晏去後運鹽之權又復分散，湊不出應有的賞賜。官軍在邊鎮既無糧又無錢，飢兵一旦進了有城有庫的都城，飢寒本身就會變成反叛的燃料。
causeEn: The direct cause of the outbreak was that a frontier army summoned on short notice could find no food in the capital. In the autumn of the first year of Xingyuan the Tibetans pressed the frontier, and the court levied the Jingyuan troops to guard the capital; once they arrived, the Northern Gate guards and the imperial granaries should have taken over their supply, but the guards were slow to move out, the treasuries had been emptied by the crisis at Fengtian and by the court's repeated flights, and the supervising eunuchs and the circuit commissioner blamed each other, so the soldiers lay for days in the wards without hot food and their resentment grew to breaking point. On the night itself men who went into the city looking for grain were refused, beat on the palisades and drums, and in a moment the whole thing dissolved; the central authority and the palace guard collapsed together. Deeper down lies the institutional cause: after the An Lushan rebellion the militia system had decayed, the frontier armies depended entirely on recruitment and on tuntian farming, and Jingyuan, a poor circuit at the edge of the desert, had so little water and so little land that even in good years it barely fed itself and in bad years had to look to transport from the interior. Since the two-tax law the court's military expenditure had swollen, with campaigns against Hebei and against the Tibetans running at the same time; the Department of State Finance was chronically in deficit, and although the salt monopoly had been reformed under Liu Yan, after his removal the conduct of the salt transport fell apart again, so the promised rewards could not be paid. With neither grain nor money in the frontier camps, hungry soldiers who once reached a city full of granaries turned hunger itself into the fuel of rebellion.
impact: 這場兵變在唐代中期是一次傷筋動骨的打擊。第一，京師再度淪陷、天子再度出奔，從此出奔不再是國難的例外而是常態，中央對地方的威信與對藩鎮的約束力一併下降。第二，它開了一個惡劣的榜樣：軍隊以饑為由譁變，攻入都城，擁立舊日將領另建名號；河北、淮西、河東一帶的藩鎮此後群起效尤，兵變與稱帝接踵而至，唐廷要再用兵鎮自己的兵鎮，就更加步履維艱。第三，財政與軍制被迫改弦。度支在關中存糧不足、漕運艱難的局面下整頓轉運，陸贄在行在屢次建言整頓兩稅之外的附加，限制鹽利與斂括；朝廷亦以護軍宿衛京師取代原有的北衙禁軍體系，中唐的神策由此成形，而禁軍的統屬卻逐步落到宦官手中，成為唐末宦官掌軍、藩鎮尾大不掉的一重伏筆。第四，兵變同時消耗了西北邊防，吐蕃趁關中空虛再犯邊塞，關中丁口再受戰亂與饑荒衝擊，國家財賦重心愈發偏重江淮，江南的繁榮與北方的凋敝愈見分明。
impactEn: For the middle Tang this mutiny was a blow to the vitals. First, the capital fell a second time and the emperor fled a second time; from then on flight was no longer an exception in a national emergency but a normal state of affairs, and the court's authority over the provinces and its power over the provincial commands declined together. Second, it set a malignant example: an army mutinies on the grounds of hunger, forces its way into the capital, and sets up some former commander under a new title; the circuits of Hebei, of Huaixi and of Hedong afterwards copied the pattern, and mutinies and proclamations followed one another, leaving the court ever more unable to use one circuit's soldiers against another. Third, the fiscal and military systems had to be re-tuned. With granaries in Guanzhong short and river transport difficult, the Department of State Finance reorganised the movement of grain, and Lu Zhi from the temporary court repeatedly urged that the surcharges laid on top of the two-tax law be regularised and that the salt revenues and the extra levies be curbed; the court also replaced the old Northern Gate guard system with a royal guard corps for the capital, out of which the mid-Tang shence evolved, yet command over the guard drifted into the hands of the eunuchs, laying one of the seeds of eunuch control of the army and of overmighty provincial commands at the end of the dynasty. Fourth, the mutiny drained the northwestern frontier at the same time, the Tibetans took advantage of an empty Guanzhong to press the border again, the population of Guanzhong was struck once more by war and famine, and the fiscal centre of the state leaned more and more heavily on the Jiangnan, so that the prosperity of the south and the desolation of the north grew ever more sharply contrasted.
result: 就眼前的勝負而言，叛軍是得手而不得久。五千缺糧的邊軍在十月的夜裡攻入長安，焚宮闕、掠府庫，擾動京師近九個月，把唐代兩京的尊嚴再踏一遍；朱泚稱帝建燕，卻只控制關中一隅，各道節度使多不奉詔，燕軍的糧源全靠劫掠，士卒掠盡便無以為繼。九月，河中、邠寧與關內各鎮兵入京師，朱泚焚宮室西走奉天，被段秀實追及，陣前擊殺，燕政權覆亡。善後方面，姚令言已死於亂軍，朝廷不再信任舊涇原將吏，改以段秀實收拾殘部，餘眾分補他鎮缺額，編制重新整理；降附者或赦或收編，長安一城在兵亂後另設軍令管束士卒，禁絕劫掠，以圖恢復市易。然而根子未除：欠餉與饑荒照舊，關中倉廩空虛，一年之後李懷光又以河中兵反，德宗被迫再度播遷，涇原兵變其實只是更大一場崩潰的前奏。史家論唐之中衰，常以安史之亂、涇原之變與黃巢之亂並列，而涇原之變最令人心寒之處，在於它並非天災，而是制度失靈的直觀演示。
resultEn: In the short run the rebels won and did not last. Five thousand hungry frontier soldiers entered Chang'an on an October night, burned the palace buildings, stripped the treasuries and disturbed the capital for close to nine months, trampling once again on the dignity of the Tang capitals. Zhu Ci proclaimed himself emperor and founded the Great Yan, yet he held only a corner of Guanzhong, most circuit commissioners refused his edicts, and the Yan army lived entirely on plunder, so that once the plunder was exhausted there was nothing left to sustain it. In the ninth month the armies of Hezhong, of Binning and of the interior circuits entered the capital; Zhu Ci burned the palace buildings and fled west to Fengtian, where Duan Xiushi overtook him and killed him in the melee, and the Yan regime perished. As for the aftermath, Yao Lingyan was already dead at the hands of his own men, the court no longer trusted the old Jingyuan officers, and Duan Xiushi was set to gather up the remnants; the survivors were distributed to make good the deficits of other circuits and the establishment was reorganised; those who surrendered were pardoned or absorbed, and in the capital a separate military command was appointed to keep the soldiers from plundering so that the markets might be restored. Yet the root was not removed: arrears of pay and famine remained as before, the granaries of Guanzhong stayed empty, and within a year Li Huaiguang rebelled again with the troops of Hezhong, driving the emperor into yet another flight. The Jingyuan mutiny was in truth only the prelude to a far greater collapse. When historians set the decline of the middle Tang in order, they commonly place the An Lushan rebellion, the Jingyuan mutiny and the Huang Chao rebellion side by side, and the most chilling thing about Jingyuan is that it was no natural disaster at all but a direct demonstration of institutional failure.
